slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Inductive reasoning means making a general conjecture from a pattern in examples. It is how mathematicians discover ideas, but it never proves them.

Place points on a circle and join every pair with a chord, keeping the points so that no three chords meet at one inside point. With 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 points the circle splits into 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 regions. The pattern says 32 for 6 points, but the true answer is 31. One counterexample is enough to show a conjecture is false.

slides.html: Lena says: 2, 3, 5 and 7 are prime, so every number of the form 2n + 1 is prime. Find a counterexample.
slides.reveal: n = 4 gives 9 = 3 times 3, which is not prime. (So does n = 7, giving 15.)
